# Rework: gh-1235 — fix the red validation head (Android APK CI leg)

## Issues/Notes

- **CI failure (blocking):** the red head `d01daa7` failed the **Build Android APK (debug)** CI leg and nothing else (all test shards, analyze, web/iOS/macOS builds were green). Gradle failed while *evaluating* the new plugin dependency:
  ```text
  Build file '.../flutter_inappwebview_android-1.1.3/android/build.gradle' line: 44
  > `getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android.txt')` is no longer supported since it
    includes `-dontoptimize`, which prevents R8 from performing many optimizations.
    Instead use `getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android-optimize.txt')`...
  ```
  `flutter_inappwebview` 6.1.5 transitively pins `flutter_inappwebview_android` **1.1.3**, which still calls the proguard file name that **AGP 9** (this repo uses AGP 9.0.1 / Gradle 9.1.0, see `flutter_app/android/settings.gradle.kts`) removed.
- **First fix attempt (rejected):** overriding only `flutter_inappwebview_android: 1.2.0-beta.3` fixed Gradle evaluation but broke the app compile — the beta drags `flutter_inappwebview_platform_interface` to `1.4.0-beta.3`, against which the *stable* `flutter_inappwebview_windows 0.6.0` no longer compiles (`Target kernel_snapshot_program failed`). The packages are only coherent as a set.
- No source-code changes were needed; the wiring (`openUrlHandler`, `FaWebViewHost`, renderer host) from the original PR is correct and its tests pass unchanged.

## Approach

1. Reproduced the failure locally with the exact CI command (`flutter build apk --debug --flavor store`) — identical Gradle error (RED).
2. Bumped `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` to the coherent upstream beta set:
   - `flutter_inappwebview: ^6.1.5` → **`^6.2.0-beta.3`** — the first published line whose Android build script evaluates under AGP 9 (`proguard-android-optimize.txt`, Java 17, androidx bumps). `6.2.0-beta.3` resolves the matching betas of every federated impl (`platform_interface 1.4.0-beta.3`, android/ios/macos/web `1.2.0-beta.3`, windows `0.7.0-beta.3`, linux `0.1.0-beta.1`) — the combination upstream itself ships and tests, unlike the mixed stable/beta graph.
   - Documented in the pubspec comment and `AGENTS.md` that this is temporary: return to `^6.1.x` (or newer stable) once 6.2.0 stable ships.
3. `flutter pub get` regenerated `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.cc` / `generated_plugins.cmake` — the beta adds the previously absent Linux implementation; the registrant updates match the already-committed macOS/Windows ones from the original PR (plugin class names `InAppWebViewFlutterPlugin` / `FlutterInappwebviewWindowsPluginCApi` are unchanged, so those registrants stay valid).
4. Housekeeping: removed a stray junk file (`[REDACTED:Credential` newline-named placeholder accidentally created by the shell redaction layer and auto-committed by the WIP auto-save job) from the index and disk.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` — `flutter_inappwebview` bumped to `^6.2.0-beta.3` with a comment explaining the AGP 9 constraint and the removal marker.
- `AGENTS.md` — the `flutter_app/lib/apps/` entry now records the 6.2.0-beta.3 pin and why (1.1.x evaluates a proguard file AGP 9 removed).
- `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.cc`, `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugins.cmake` — pub-generated: register `flutter_inappwebview_linux` (new with the 6.2.0-beta line).
- (staged) deletion of the accidental `flutter_app/[REDACTED:Credential` junk file.

## Test Coverage

This was a **build/CI failure** (Gradle plugin evaluation + Dart kernel snapshot), not a runtime bug — the reproduction and verification *is* the failing build leg itself; there is no unit-test seam for it. Verified locally on the exact CI matrix entries:

| Check | CI leg it mirrors | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `flutter build apk --debug --flavor store` | Build Android APK (debug) — the red leg | ✅ (was failing with the proguard error before the fix) |
| `flutter build web --debug` | Build web (debug) | ✅ |

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

    includes `-dontoptimize`, which prevents R8 from performing many optimizations.
    Instead use `getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android-optimize.txt')`...
  ```

The packages are only coherent as a set.
- No source-code changes were needed; the wiring (`openUrlHandler`, `FaWebViewHost`, renderer host) from the original PR is correct and its tests pass unchanged.

## Approach

1. Reproduced the failure locally with the exact CI command (`flutter build apk --debug --flavor store`) — identical Gradle error (RED).
2. Bumped `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` to the coherent upstream beta set:

3. `flutter pub get` regenerated `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.cc` / `generated_plugins.cmake` — the beta adds the previously absent Linux implementation; the registrant updates match the already-committed macOS/Windows ones from the original PR (plugin class names `InAppWebViewFlutterPlugin` / `FlutterInappwebviewWindowsPluginCApi` are unchanged, so those registrants stay valid).
4. Housekeeping: removed a stray junk file (`[REDACTED:Credential` newline-named placeholder accidentally created by the shell redaction layer and auto-committed by the WIP auto-save job) from the index and disk.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` — `flutter_inappwebview` bumped to `^6.2.0-beta.3` with a comment explaining the AGP 9 constraint and the removal marker.
- `AGENTS.md` — the `flutter_app/lib/apps/` entry now records the 6.2.0-beta.3 pin and why (1.1.x evaluates a proguard file AGP 9 removed).
- `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.cc`, `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugins.cmake` — pub-generated: register `flutter_inappwebview_linux` (new with the 6.2.0-beta line).

This was a **build/CI failure** (Gradle plugin evaluation + Dart kernel snapshot), not a runtime bug — the reproduction and verification *is* the failing build leg itself; there is no unit-test seam for it. Verified locally on the exact CI matrix entries:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

1. Reproduced the failure locally with the exact CI command (`flutter build apk --debug --flavor store`) — identical Gradle error (RED).

3. `flutter pub get` regenerated `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.cc` / `generated_plugins.cmake` — the beta adds the previously absent Linux implementation; the registrant updates match the already-committed macOS/Windows ones from the original PR (plugin class names `InAppWebViewFlutterPlugin` / `FlutterInappwebviewWindowsPluginCApi` are unchanged, so those registrants stay valid).
4. Housekeeping: removed a stray junk file (`[REDACTED:Credential` newline-named placeholder accidentally created by the shell redaction layer and auto-committed by the WIP auto-save job) from the index and disk.

+    
+    override init(){
+        super.init()
+    }

+    override func getRealSettings(obj: WebAuthenticationSession?) -> [String: Any?] {
+        var realOptions: [String: Any?] = toMap()

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

# flutter_inappwebview_macos (vendored)

Verbatim copy of the published `flutter_inappwebview_macos` **1.2.0-beta.3**
(pub.dev, MIT — see `LICENSE`), required by the coherent
`flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 set (gh-1235).

**Single change vs upstream** (both macOS deployment-floor declarations
raised from 10.14 to 14.0, the app's own minimum):

- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos/Package.swift` — `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("14.0")`
- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos.podspec` — `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` → `'14.0'`

Why: upstream declares a 10.14 floor, but
`Sources/flutter_inappwebview_macos/WebAuthenticationSession/WebAuthenticationSession.swift`
marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the
`ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding` conformance fails to compile
at the 10.14 target (both the SwiftPM and the CocoaPods path). Upstream
master still carries the bug — no fixed release or commit to pin to, hence
the vendor.

**Drop procedure**: once upstream releases a version whose Package.swift /
podspec minimum is ≥ 10.15, delete this directory and the
`flutter_inappwebview_macos` entry in
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `dependency_overrides`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

# flutter_inappwebview_macos (vendored)

Verbatim copy of the published `flutter_inappwebview_macos` **1.2.0-beta.3**
(pub.dev, MIT — see `LICENSE`), required by the coherent
`flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 set (gh-1235).

**Single change vs upstream** (both macOS deployment-floor declarations
raised from 10.14 to 14.0, the app's own minimum):

- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos/Package.swift` — `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("14.0")`
- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos.podspec` — `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` → `'14.0'`

Why: upstream declares a 10.14 floor, but
`Sources/flutter_inappwebview_macos/WebAuthenticationSession/WebAuthenticationSession.swift`
marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the
`ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding` conformance fails to compile
at the 10.14 target (both the SwiftPM and the CocoaPods path). Upstream
master still carries the bug — no fixed release or commit to pin to, hence
the vendor.

**Drop procedure**: once upstream releases a version whose Package.swift /
podspec minimum is ≥ 10.15, delete this directory and the
`flutter_inappwebview_macos` entry in
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `dependency_overrides`.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

# Rework: gh-1235 — fix the red validation head (Android APK CI leg)

## Issues/Notes

- **CI failure (blocking):** the red head `d01daa7` failed the **Build Android APK (debug)** CI leg and nothing else (all test shards, analyze, web/iOS/macOS builds were green). Gradle failed while *evaluating* the new plugin dependency:
  ```text
  Build file '.../flutter_inappwebview_android-1.1.3/android/build.gradle' line: 44
  > `getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android.txt')` is no longer supported since it
    includes `-dontoptimize`, which prevents R8 from performing many optimizations.
    Instead use `getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android-optimize.txt')`...
  ```
  `flutter_inappwebview` 6.1.5 transitively pins `flutter_inappwebview_android` **1.1.3**, which still calls the proguard file name that **AGP 9** (this repo uses AGP 9.0.1 / Gradle 9.1.0, see `flutter_app/android/settings.gradle.kts`) removed.
- **First fix attempt (rejected):** overriding only `flutter_inappwebview_android: 1.2.0-beta.3` fixed Gradle evaluation but broke the app compile — the beta drags `flutter_inappwebview_platform_interface` to `1.4.0-beta.3`, against which the *stable* `flutter_inappwebview_windows 0.6.0` no longer compiles (`Target kernel_snapshot_program failed`). The packages are only coherent as a set.
- No source-code changes were needed; the wiring (`openUrlHandler`, `FaWebViewHost`, renderer host) from the original PR is correct and its tests pass unchanged.

## Approach

1. Reproduced the failure locally with the exact CI command (`flutter build apk --debug --flavor store`) — identical Gradle error (RED).
2. Bumped `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` to the coherent upstream beta set:
   - `flutter_inappwebview: ^6.1.5` → **`^6.2.0-beta.3`** — the first published line whose Android build script evaluates under AGP 9 (`proguard-android-optimize.txt`, Java 17, androidx bumps). `6.2.0-beta.3` resolves the matching betas of every federated impl (`platform_interface 1.4.0-beta.3`, android/ios/macos/web `1.2.0-beta.3`, windows `0.7.0-beta.3`, linux `0.1.0-beta.1`) — the combination upstream itself ships and tests, unlike the mixed stable/beta graph.
   - Documented in the pubspec comment and `AGENTS.md` that this is temporary: return to `^6.1.x` (or newer stable) once 6.2.0 stable ships.
3. `flutter pub get` regenerated `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.cc` / `generated_plugins.cmake` — the beta adds the previously absent Linux implementation; the registrant updates match the already-committed macOS/Windows ones from the original PR (plugin class names `InAppWebViewFlutterPlugin` / `FlutterInappwebviewWindowsPluginCApi` are unchanged, so those registrants stay valid).
4. Housekeeping: removed a stray junk file (`[REDACTED:Credential` newline-named placeholder accidentally created by the shell redaction layer and auto-committed by the WIP auto-save job) from the index and disk.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` — `flutter_inappwebview` bumped to `^6.2.0-beta.3` with a comment explaining the AGP 9 constraint and the removal marker.
- `AGENTS.md` — the `flutter_app/lib/apps/` entry now records the 6.2.0-beta.3 pin and why (1.1.x evaluates a proguard file AGP 9 removed).
- `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.cc`, `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugins.cmake` — pub-generated: register `flutter_inappwebview_linux` (new with the 6.2.0-beta line).
- (staged) deletion of the accidental `flutter_app/[REDACTED:Credential` junk file.

## Test Coverage

This was a **build/CI failure** (Gradle plugin evaluation + Dart kernel snapshot), not a runtime bug — the reproduction and verification *is* the failing build leg itself; there is no unit-test seam for it. Verified locally on the exact CI matrix entries:

| Check | CI leg it mirrors | Result |

| `flutter build apk --debug --flavor store` | Build Android APK (debug) — the red leg | ✅ (was failing with the proguard error before the fix) |
| `flutter build web --debug` | Build web (debug) | ✅ |

- iOS/macOS/Windows build legs cannot run on this Linux host, but the beta set is the upstream-coherent combination (stable/beta mixes demonstrably fail the Dart compile, which is why the umbrella moved as a whole), and plugin class names referenced by the committed registrants are unchanged.

# flutter_inappwebview_macos (vendored)

Verbatim copy of the published `flutter_inappwebview_macos` **1.2.0-beta.3**
(pub.dev, MIT — see `LICENSE`), required by the coherent
`flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 set (gh-1235).

**Single change vs upstream** (both macOS deployment-floor declarations
raised from 10.14 to 14.0, the app's own minimum):

- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos/Package.swift` — `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("14.0")`
- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos.podspec` — `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` → `'14.0'`

Why: upstream declares a 10.14 floor, but
`Sources/flutter_inappwebview_macos/WebAuthenticationSession/WebAuthenticationSession.swift`
marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the
`ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding` conformance fails to compile
at the 10.14 target (both the SwiftPM and the CocoaPods path). Upstream
master still carries the bug — no fixed release or commit to pin to, hence
the vendor.

**Drop procedure**: once upstream releases a version whose Package.swift /
podspec minimum is ≥ 10.15, delete this directory and the
`flutter_inappwebview_macos` entry in
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `dependency_overrides`.
---
9:        .macOS("14.0"),
25:  s.platform = :osx, '14.0'

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

+//
+//  WebAuthenticationSessionSettings.swift
+//  flutter_inappwebview
+//
+//  Created by Lorenzo Pichilli on 08/05/22.
+//
+
+import Foundation
+import AuthenticationServices
+import SafariServices
+
+@objcMembers
+public class WebAuthenticationSessionSettings: ISettings<WebAuthenticationSession> {
+    
+    var prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession = false
+    
+    override init(){
+        super.init()
+    }
+    
+    override func getRealSettings(obj: WebAuthenticationSession?) -> [String: Any?] {
+        var realOptions: [String: Any?] = toMap()
+        if #available(macOS 10.15, *), let session = obj?.session as? ASWebAuthenticationSession {
+            realOptions["prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession"] = session.prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession
+        }
+        return realOptions
+    }
+}

# flutter_inappwebview_macos (vendored)

Verbatim copy of the published `flutter_inappwebview_macos` **1.2.0-beta.3**
(pub.dev, MIT — see `LICENSE`), required by the coherent
`flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 set (gh-1235).

**Single change vs upstream** (both macOS deployment-floor declarations
raised from 10.14 to 14.0, the app's own minimum):

- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos/Package.swift` — `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("14.0")`
- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos.podspec` — `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` → `'14.0'`

Why: upstream declares a 10.14 floor, but
`Sources/flutter_inappwebview_macos/WebAuthenticationSession/WebAuthenticationSession.swift`
marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the
`ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding` conformance fails to compile
at the 10.14 target (both the SwiftPM and the CocoaPods path). Upstream
master still carries the bug — no fixed release or commit to pin to, hence
the vendor.

**Drop procedure**: once upstream releases a version whose Package.swift /
podspec minimum is ≥ 10.15, delete this directory and the
`flutter_inappwebview_macos` entry in
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `dependency_overrides`.
---
9:        .macOS("14.0"),
25:  s.platform = :osx, '14.0'

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

- **CI failure (blocking):** the red head `d01daa7` failed the **Build Android APK (debug)** CI leg and nothing else (all test shards, analyze, web/iOS/macOS builds were green). Gradle failed while *evaluating* the new plugin dependency:
  ```text
  Build file '.../flutter_inappwebview_android-1.1.3/android/build.gradle' line: 44
  > `getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android.txt')` is no longer supported since it
    includes `-dontoptimize`, which prevents R8 from performing many optimizations.
    Instead use `getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android-optimize.txt')`...
  ```
  `flutter_inappwebview` 6.1.5 transitively pins `flutter_inappwebview_android` **1.1.3**, which still calls the proguard file name that **AGP 9** (this repo uses AGP 9.0.1 / Gradle 9.1.0, see `flutter_app/android/settings.gradle.kts`) removed.
- **First fix attempt (rejected):** overriding only `flutter_inappwebview_android: 1.2.0-beta.3` fixed Gradle evaluation but broke the app compile — the beta drags `flutter_inappwebview_platform_interface` to `1.4.0-beta.3`, against which the *stable* `flutter_inappwebview_windows 0.6.0` no longer compiles (`Target kernel_snapshot_program failed`). The packages are only coherent as a set.
- No source-code changes were needed; the wiring (`openUrlHandler`, `FaWebViewHost`, renderer host) from the original PR is correct and its tests pass unchanged.

## Approach

1. Reproduced the failure locally with the exact CI command (`flutter build apk --debug --flavor store`) — identical Gradle error (RED).
2. Bumped `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` to the coherent upstream beta set:
   - `flutter_inappwebview: ^6.1.5` → **`^6.2.0-beta.3`** — the first published line whose Android build script evaluates under AGP 9 (`proguard-android-optimize.txt`, Java 17, androidx bumps). `6.2.0-beta.3` resolves the matching betas of every federated impl (`platform_interface 1.4.0-beta.3`, android/ios/macos/web `1.2.0-beta.3`, windows `0.7.0-beta.3`, linux `0.1.0-beta.1`) — the combination upstream itself ships and tests, unlike the mixed stable/beta graph.
   - Documented in the pubspec comment and `AGENTS.md` that this is temporary: return to `^6.1.x` (or newer stable) once 6.2.0 stable ships.
3. `flutter pub get` regenerated `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.cc` / `generated_plugins.cmake` — the beta adds the previously absent Linux implementation; the registrant updates match the already-committed macOS/Windows ones from the original PR (plugin class names `InAppWebViewFlutterPlugin` / `FlutterInappwebviewWindowsPluginCApi` are unchanged, so those registrants stay valid).
4. Housekeeping: removed a stray junk file (`[REDACTED:Credential` newline-named placeholder accidentally created by the shell redaction layer and auto-committed by the WIP auto-save job) from the index and disk.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` — `flutter_inappwebview` bumped to `^6.2.0-beta.3` with a comment explaining the AGP 9 constraint and the removal marker.
- `AGENTS.md` — the `flutter_app/lib/apps/` entry now records the 6.2.0-beta.3 pin and why (1.1.x evaluates a proguard file AGP 9 removed).
- `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.cc`, `flutter_app/linux/flutter/generated_plugins.cmake` — pub-generated: register `flutter_inappwebview_linux` (new with the 6.2.0-beta line).
- (staged) deletion of the accidental `flutter_app/[REDACTED:Credential` junk file.

This was a **build/CI failure** (Gradle plugin evaluation + Dart kernel snapshot), not a runtime bug — the reproduction and verification *is* the failing build leg itself; there is no unit-test seam for it. Verified locally on the exact CI matrix entries:

+//

+//  Created by Lorenzo Pichilli on 08/05/22.

+
+import Foundation
+import AuthenticationServices
+import SafariServices
+
+@objcMembers
+public class WebAuthenticationSessionSettings: ISettings<WebAuthenticationSession> {
+    
+    var prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession = false
+    
+    override init(){
+        super.init()
+    }
+    
+    override func getRealSettings(obj: WebAuthenticationSession?) -> [String: Any?] {
+        var realOptions: [String: Any?] = toMap()
+        if #available(macOS 10.15, *), let session = obj?.session as? ASWebAuthenticationSession {
+            realOptions["prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession"] = session.prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession
+        }
+        return realOptions
+    }
+}

(pub.dev, MIT — see `LICENSE`), required by the coherent

**Single change vs upstream** (both macOS deployment-floor declarations
raised from 10.14 to 14.0, the app's own minimum):

- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos/Package.swift` — `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("14.0")`
- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos.podspec` — `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` → `'14.0'`

at the 10.14 target (both the SwiftPM and the CocoaPods path). Upstream
master still carries the bug — no fixed release or commit to pin to, hence
the vendor.

**Drop procedure**: once upstream releases a version whose Package.swift /
podspec minimum is ≥ 10.15, delete this directory and the
`flutter_inappwebview_macos` entry in
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `dependency_overrides`.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

```mermaid

  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]

  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH

(pub.dev, MIT — see `LICENSE`), required by the coherent

**Single change vs upstream** (both macOS deployment-floor declarations
raised from 10.14 to 14.0, the app's own minimum):

- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos/Package.swift` — `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("14.0")`
- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos.podspec` — `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` → `'14.0'`

Why: upstream declares a 10.14 floor, but
`Sources/flutter_inappwebview_macos/WebAuthenticationSession/WebAuthenticationSession.swift`
marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the
`ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding` conformance fails to compile
at the 10.14 target (both the SwiftPM and the CocoaPods path). Upstream
master still carries the bug — no fixed release or commit to pin to, hence
the vendor.

**Drop procedure**: once upstream releases a version whose Package.swift /
podspec minimum is ≥ 10.15, delete this directory and the
`flutter_inappwebview_macos` entry in
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `dependency_overrides`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

# flutter_inappwebview_macos (vendored)

Verbatim copy of the published `flutter_inappwebview_macos` **1.2.0-beta.3**
(pub.dev, MIT — see `LICENSE`), required by the coherent
`flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 set (gh-1235).

**Single change vs upstream** (both macOS deployment-floor declarations
raised from 10.14 to 14.0, the app's own minimum):

- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos/Package.swift` — `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("14.0")`
- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos.podspec` — `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` → `'14.0'`

Why: upstream declares a 10.14 floor, but
`Sources/flutter_inappwebview_macos/WebAuthenticationSession/WebAuthenticationSession.swift`
marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the
`ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding` conformance fails to compile
at the 10.14 target (both the SwiftPM and the CocoaPods path). Upstream
master still carries the bug — no fixed release or commit to pin to, hence
the vendor.

**Drop procedure**: once upstream releases a version whose Package.swift /
podspec minimum is ≥ 10.15, delete this directory and the
`flutter_inappwebview_macos` entry in
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `dependency_overrides`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

+import Foundation

+
+@objcMembers

+    
+    var prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession = false
+    
+    override init(){
+        super.init()
+    }
+    
+    override func getRealSettings(obj: WebAuthenticationSession?) -> [String: Any?] {
+        var realOptions: [String: Any?] = toMap()
+        if #available(macOS 10.15, *), let session = obj?.session as? ASWebAuthenticationSession {

+        }
+        return realOptions
+    }

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: stale guard rationale — 6.2.0-beta.3 *does* ship Linux/Windows implementations**

The doc comment says "Linux/Windows (the plugin has no support there)", but that was true of the 6.1.x line this PR originally targeted. The coherent 6.2.0-beta.3 set this PR landed on adds `flutter_inappwebview_linux` 0.1.0-beta.1 and `flutter_inappwebview_windows` 0.7.0-beta.3 — the PR itself commits the regenerated Linux registrant registering `flutter_inappwebview_linux`. So the platform guard is now a deliberate choice to keep the renderer placeholder, but the stated reason is wrong, and the committed Linux plugin registration is dead weight.

Either:
- keep the placeholder deliberately (beta Linux/Windows impls are incomplete) and fix the comment to say *why* ("beta linux/windows impls not yet exercised by this host"), or
- extend the switch to Linux/Windows and drop the now-dead Linux registrant wiring.

As written, the comment will mislead the next person into thinking the registrant entry is load-bearing.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `javaScriptEnabled: onMessage != null` breaks JS-dependent pages without a message handler**

A `webView` node that doesn't declare `onMessage` gets a webview with JavaScript fully disabled — most real web content (SPA shells, client-rendered docs, pages that need JS even to lay out) will render blank or broken. The `onMessage` gating only needs to control whether the `jsr` bridge handler is *registered* (`onWebViewCreated` already returns early when `onMessage == null`); it doesn't need to disable the page's own JavaScript.

Consider `javaScriptEnabled: true` unconditionally (it's the upstream example host's behavior) and keep the bridge registration as the only gated part. If disabling JS is an intentional hardening choice for message-less embeds, it's worth a comment saying so — the current code reads like an oversight.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

  error: protocol 'ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding' requires
  'presentationAnchor(for:)' to be available in macOS 10.14 and newer

- **Root cause:** the beta plugin's podspec declares `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` while its Swift marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the pod target compiles at 10.14 and the protocol conformance fails. - Everything else on the head was green, including the previously red `build-android` leg, confirming the round-1 dependency fix held.

+import Foundation

+    
+    var prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession = false
+    
+    override init(){
+        super.init()
+    }
+    
+    override func getRealSettings(obj: WebAuthenticationSession?) -> [String: Any?] {
+        var realOptions: [String: Any?] = toMap()
+        if #available(macOS 10.15, *), let session = obj?.session as? ASWebAuthenticationSession {
+            realOptions["prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession"] = session.prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession
+        }
+        return realOptions
+    }

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

  'presentationAnchor(for:)' to be available in macOS 10.14 and newer
  ```
- **Root cause:** the beta plugin's podspec declares `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` while its Swift marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the pod target compiles at 10.14 and the protocol conformance fails. This is an **upstream bug** — I verified `master` (upstream) still carries the same podspec minimum and annotation, so a git pin is not an alternative.
- The failing Swift compile line was `-target arm64-apple-macos10.14` while the app itself targets macOS 14.0 (`platform :osx, '14.0'` in `flutter_app/macos/Podfile`) — the pod just inherits the plugin's own (too-low) minimum.
- Everything else on the head was green, including the previously red `build-android` leg, confirming the round-1 dependency fix held.

## Approach

1. Raised the `flutter_inappwebview_macos` pod target's `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` to **14.0** (the app's own floor) in the existing `post_install` hook in `flutter_app/macos/Podfile` — same place the Podfile already patches build settings for other plugins (wasm_run, flutter_gemma). # flutter_inappwebview_macos (vendored)

Verbatim copy of the published `flutter_inappwebview_macos` **1.2.0-beta.3**
(pub.dev, MIT — see `LICENSE`), required by the coherent
`flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 set (gh-1235).

**Single change vs upstream** (both macOS deployment-floor declarations
raised from 10.14 to 14.0, the app's own minimum):

- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos/Package.swift` — `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("14.0")`
- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos.podspec` — `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` → `'14.0'`

Why: upstream declares a 10.14 floor, but
`Sources/flutter_inappwebview_macos/WebAuthenticationSession/WebAuthenticationSession.swift`
marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the
`ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding` conformance fails to compile
at the 10.14 target (both the SwiftPM and the CocoaPods path). Upstream
master still carries the bug — no fixed release or commit to pin to, hence

If disabling JS is an intentional hardening choice for message-less embeds, it's worth a comment saying so — the current code reads like an oversight.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1238
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1238
- **Title**: gh-1235 Wire jsr.openUrl + webView host into the app JS engine (js_widget_runtime = 0.4.154)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1235` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 172
- **Additions**: +21269
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T16:20:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:35:07Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Wired the two web capabilities shipped in js_widget_runtime 0.4.154 into the app JS engine: `jsr.openUrl(url)` opens URLs in the host browser via `url_launcher` (`LaunchMode.externalApplication`, `{'__error': ...}` rejections), and `webView` nodes render through a new `FaWebViewHost` (`flutter_app/lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart`) backed by `flutter_inappwebview` with the system default data store (no incognito). `js_widget_runtime` bumped to `^0.4.154` and git-pinned to upstream commit `bd1e7c2` until the hosted release lands.

### Key decisions
- `FaWebViewHost` is passed to BOTH the `JsRuntimeConfig` (js_app_engine.dart) and the `JsonWidgetRenderer` (js_app_view.dart), matching the shared-host pattern of `js3dHost`.
- `createFaWebViewHost()` guards by platform: real webview on iOS/Android/macOS, renderer placeholder (null) on Linux/Windows/web — the plugin has no Linux support.
- `JsAppEngine.webViewHost` / `JsAppView.webViewHost` are injectable seams (same convention as `mediaHost`/`mapTileProvider`) so tests stay off the native plugin.
- Plugin registrant updates (macOS/Windows) are pub-generated; the pubspec override mirrors the existing `flutter_js` fork pin and is marked for removal once hosted 0.4.154+ is out.
- Tests: `fa_webview_host_test.dart` (host construction incl. default-data-store settings, platform guard, webView node through the renderer, `{value: msg}` forwarding, placeholder fallback) and `js_app_open_url_test.dart` (success ×2 URLs, cannot-launch rejection, launch-failed rejection via the `url_launcher_platform_interface` mock seam).

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter test test/apps/fa_webview_host_test.dart test/apps/js_app_open_url_test.dart
flutter test test/apps/
```
The openUrl engine tests boot the real QuickJS bridge — on hosts without `libquickjs_c_bridge_plugin.so` they skip with the standard issue #184 reason (pass when run with the flutter_js git package's `linux/shared` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS["jsr.openUrl(url) / webView node"] --> ENG["JsAppEngine (JsRuntimeConfig)"]
  ENG -->|"openUrlHandler"| UL["url_launcher (externalApplication)"]
  ENG -->|"webViewHost"| WVH["FaWebViewHost (flutter_inappwebview, default data store)"]
  VIEW["JsAppView (JsonWidgetRenderer)"] -->|"webViewHost"| WVH
  WVH -.->|"linux/windows/web"| PH["renderer placeholder"]
```

</details>

  error: protocol 'ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding' requires
  'presentationAnchor(for:)' to be available in macOS 10.14 and newer

- **Root cause:** the beta plugin's podspec declares `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` while its Swift marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the pod target compiles at 10.14 and the protocol conformance fails. - Everything else on the head was green, including the previously red `build-android` leg, confirming the round-1 dependency fix held.

+import Foundation

+    
+    var prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession = false
+    
+    override init(){
+        super.init()
+    }
+    
+    override func getRealSettings(obj: WebAuthenticationSession?) -> [String: Any?] {
+        var realOptions: [String: Any?] = toMap()
+        if #available(macOS 10.15, *), let session = obj?.session as? ASWebAuthenticationSession {
+            realOptions["prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession"] = session.prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession
+        }
+        return realOptions
+    }
